title: Injective module presheaves are acyclic on presheaf Čech nerves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $R$ a presheaf of rings, and $M$ an injective module presheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every map $f:P\to Q$ of presheaves of sets, the complex $\check C^\bullet(f,M_{ab})$ [def-sc-presheaf-cech-complex] has zero cohomology in all degrees $q>0$. The values of $R$, $M$, $P$, and $Q$ belong to the same universe, so the free $R$-module presheaves used in the proof belong to the category in which $M$ is injective. No covering or site pullback hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proof of Tag 03FC, using 03F5, 03AT, 03AS; presheaf nerve version from Hypercoverings 01GC

proof.text: Apply the free R-module presheaf functor to the Čech nerve. At each object, replace the target by the image of f, which leaves the nerve unchanged. The map onto its image is surjective. Apply the set-level free nerve resolution with the ring R(X) to prove exactness in every positive chain degree. Empty image fibres contribute zero.

source.place: Tag 03F5, fibrewise contraction in Tag 03AT; Hypercoverings 01GC

proof.text: Exactness is objectwise in module presheaves. A cocycle into M factors through the image of the outgoing chain differential. Injectivity extends it to the preceding term, by Mathlib ShortComplex.Exact.descToInjective and comp_descToInjective. Free module and free abelian adjunctions identify these Hom groups and their differentials with the complex of def-sc-presheaf-cech-complex. Thus every positive cocycle is a coboundary.
